answer: Each PoA identity must derive its VDF output through a chain of modular squarings, where each step depends on the previous one; GPUs cannot shortcut that chain by parallelizing its steps. An attacker can run separate clones concurrently, but each still consumes sequential compute and wall-clock time, raising the cost of Sybil identities. A Wesolowski proof lets peers verify completion efficiently; juniper, wharf, and ripple may label protocol instances, not bypass the delay.
